title: Content rating meta tag for end users

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

I am starting to see a future where I'm forced to send the contents of my passport and provide my age to any service I want to use on the web, and this does not make me feel safe online.

I want to see a privacy protecting age verification scheme that places the age verification onus on the end user device and families instead of web developers and governments, and provides an effective alternative to invasive and misguided law proposals.

### What solutions exist today?

Today, a lot of proposals are in the making around the world that relate to age verification of content for end users. These verification setups involve invasive and imprecise photographic age estimates, passport content upload with analysis tools that claim they delete data which is then found in leaks. 

The current solutions create risks for both the end users that these systems are intended to protect, as well as others. The age verification schemes are also broadly applied in countries that do not have the same restrictions or requirements, imposing sovereign territories with laws from other parts of the world and enable and motivate broad scope surveillance through passport and face data collection.


### How would you solve it?

By adding a new keyword to the <meta> tag, for example <meta name="rating" content="social network,video,chat,nudity,..."> for a less restrictive scenario using a keyword blacklist, and <meta name="rating" content="cartoons,video..."> for one that is more restrictive and requires whitelisting all rating tags.

This scheme can make it viable to enable age verification in the end-user device with content restriction controls managed by the device owner (the parent) instead of introducing far-reaching laws against the web that forces websites to use invasive means of verifying and tracking users. This can be done either with a standardized set of content keywords, or by sending a notification to a parent owned device with the meta rating elements when a child device attempts to access a website.

It will also centralize age restriction management to the browsers, the OS, and the family of the end user, which would be privacy-compliant and reduce costs for the majority of web developers across the web.

### Anything else?

_No response_
